claims.claim: Cloudflare introduced Durable Objects in closed beta on September 28, 2020, with unique identity and private durable state.
Requests for an object identity reach one active location, allowing related clients to coordinate through it.
Inference: One object identity does not imply that all asynchronous handler operations form one atomic transaction.
Independent objects partition an application into logical coordination units; one busy object remains one authority.
workerd was released as an Apache-licensed open-source runtime beta in September 2022.
Cloudflare described the earlier self-hosted Durable Objects implementation as single-instance and its production routing as unsuitable for ordinary self-hosters.
The September 2024 SQLite-in-Durable-Objects release embedded SQL beside object execution; local query access does not establish remote durability.
Celld uses compute nodes, SQLite-backed cells, shared bucket storage, and conditional ownership assignment.
Deno and Cloudflare announced the team joining Cloudflare and focusing future effort on a shared self-hostable platform.
Deno announced one year of runtime fixes and security releases and six months of continued Deploy operation.
The announcement said JSR would continue operating and rusty_v8 would remain supported.
The supplied initial commit adds experimental shared-bucket clustering, forwarding, ownership and bucket-backed recovery.
The inspected October 31 workerd snapshot includes alarms and facets beyond the initial shared-bucket merge.

claims.claim: Inference: separate reads and unconditional writes allow two contenders to observe absence before either declaration is published.
Inference: an unconditional last overwrite alone cannot retract serving decisions already made by another contender.
Inference: a separate read and write do not make an atomic ownership operation; the condition must be checked by storage.
Conditional writes apply only when the storage-side precondition holds for the write.
Conditional create admits one successful creation when contenders race on an absent authority key.
Conditional overwrite rejects a stale version rather than replacing a record that changed after the read.
workerd uses an opaque Version with Guard::Match to protect replacement of an ownership record.
The workerd OwnerRecord contains node, epoch and from; from identifies the last epoch that finished opening.
The storage contract requires read-after-write consistency independently of conditional update semantics.
Celld probes conditional creation, rejection of another creation, conditional updating and rejection of a stale update.
Inference: serializing a single ownership key does not itself provide atomic application transactions across separate objects.
Inference: the application fleet relies on the object store for conditional serialization rather than implementing a separate consensus service for ownership.
Inference: moving ownership serialization to the bucket makes ownership progress depend on bucket semantics and availability.
Guarded ownership acquisition accepts one record version and directs nonowners toward the accepted live owner.

chapters.title: A lease is not a fence

claims.claim: workerd publishes node records with expires_ms and uses their expiry when deciding whether a peer is live.
The lease state machine retries failed renewals while its safety window permits and fences when that window closes.
workerd defines a 20000 ms lease, 3000 ms renewal interval, 4000 ms renewal timeout and 1000 ms retry interval.
Observed absolute bucket-clock skew greater than 2000 ms causes the workerd lease state machine to fence.
workerd derives SAFETY_MS as twice MAX_SKEW_MS, reserving a 4000 ms serving margin before expiry.
Inference from holds and before_renew: for expiry 20000 ms, serving requires time below 16000 ms and starting renewal requires time below 12000 ms.
before_renew fences a node whose previous lease cannot safely cover a renewal; a test covers a node stalled beyond its lease.
Clock skew comes from the bucket observation; Cluster::clock_skew_ms defaults an unavailable observation to zero.
Ownership takeover uses a conditional record replacement and successor increments the ownership epoch.
A superseded owner can finish an upload to its old session, but that does not establish current ownership.
Owner::push rereads current_epoch after the upload and returns Contended on epoch mismatch before slot.ack.
OwnerRecord::successor preserves from until the claimed epoch opens, retaining the last opened recovery source.
Inference: lease expiry, guarded ownership updates and post-upload epoch checks close separate replacement and acknowledgement failure windows.
Inference: failed bucket operations can prevent acknowledgements, and sustained renewal failure can fence all affected writers.
SQLite runs locally beside the object; the cluster commit path separately makes captured writes durable remotely.
A workerd cluster commit waits for bucket-backed coverage rather than treating local database completion as sufficient acknowledgement proof.
The acknowledgement watermark advances only after upload and the current-epoch check.
SQLite WAL capture observes page frames before later checkpoints copy their changes into the database file.
The workerd capture layer identifies a completed WAL transaction using the final frame database-size field.
Capture buffers frames since the previous commit and handles rollback overwriting uncommitted frames.
workerd merges captured page frames into compressed batches carrying session and sequence coverage.
Celld captures SQLite WAL changes into LTX; the inspected workerd cluster path instead uses frames.capnp.
Owner::push uploads staged changes, rereads current_epoch and only then acknowledges a matching epoch.
Workerd groups uploads and waiting callers require an acknowledgement watermark covering their own captured target.
Takeover removes nonauthoritative local database files and restores acknowledged bucket-backed history.
Celld documents durability gating for observations including response bodies, stream chunks and certain outgoing effects.
Celld gates read-only and error responses when they could expose an uncovered committed write.
Inference: a lost acknowledgement cannot establish that a write was absent, so durability alone does not guarantee exactly-once retried application effects.

chapters.title: Rebuild the room, prove the tail

claims.claim: Workerd takeover discards nonauthoritative local database state and restores the predecessor epoch from bucket history.
workerd restore starts from a snapshot and replays subsequent page-log batches rather than rerunning handlers.
Replay uses session and sequence coverage to skip already applied changes and maintain one complete history.
The workerd replay engine checks for unresolved gaps and fails if required frame coverage is missing.
workerd reads compressed content through the decoder checksum check; data detection is distinct from recreating missing bytes.
Compaction uploads the replacement snapshot before deleting the covered old files.
workerd recovers state and uploads its starting snapshot before conditionally opening the claimed epoch.
Celld v0.6.3 defaults to fleet durability and may acknowledge follower-durable writes before their bucket upload completes.
A celld fleet proof uses one or two other follower nodes and requires the participating followers to fsync the write.
Without an ensemble, celld preserves correctness by using bucket proofs; an additional follower can provide another copy.
Celld cold activation must recover the predecessor node-log acknowledged tail before restoring cell state.
Celld takeover fences the old log session, seals reachable followers, uploads retained data and marks the record sealed before restore.
Celld recovery can block on follower errors, damaged or incomplete ranges and other inability to certify a complete retained tail.
Inference: workerd bucket proofs and celld follower proofs require different recovery paths because they acknowledge bytes in different locations.
In workerd bucket-proof operation, bucket failure prevents new upload-backed acknowledgements and sustained lease failure fences serving.
Celld documents that ignored conditional-write conditions can permit two owners, violating its required storage contract.
Celld prohibits lifecycle deletion or overwrite of reserved protocol data needed to fence and restore cells.
Inference: local SQL and the remote upload plus authority check are separate portions of workerd acknowledgement latency.
Celld describes follower fsync proofs as a lower-latency alternative to bucket round trips while requiring retained follower data for recovery.
Current workerd cluster tests cover an alarm running on a survivor after the owning process is killed.

claims.claim: workerd is intended for self-hosted application execution, and celld provides SQLite-backed cells on operator-owned nodes.
Celld explicitly documents supported APIs and limits; runtime portability does not establish full hosted platform parity.
Cloudflare and Deno describe first-class self-hosting as a shared direction; the supplied workerd cluster merge is experimental.
Durable Objects debuted in 2020, workerd became open source in 2022, and SQLite-in-Durable-Objects launched in 2024.
Inference: bucket serialization and durable storage combine with runtime ownership, capture, gating and replay to provide the inspected guarantees.
Inference: portable object operation requires the runtime recovery machinery and qualified storage contract to move together.
